fr.desc: Sabri Mohamadi, Producer et Game Designer basé à Tokyo. Global Associate Producer sur Little Nightmares III, VR et mobile chez Bandai Namco Entertainment Europe. Freelance et enseignant du Bachelor au Master.
fr.cdesc: Contacter Sabri Mohamadi, Producer et Game Designer à Tokyo, pour un poste, une mission freelance ou une collab YouTube.

en.meta.title: Sabri Mohamadi | Producer & Game Designer
en.hero.lead:
Two years in the main team of Little Nightmares at Bandai Namco Entertainment Europe, as Global Associate Producer. Three games shipped, on console, PC, VR and mobile.

Today I'm a freelance Producer and Game Designer. I teach Producing, Game Design, Level Design and programming fundamentals, from first-year Bachelor to second-year Master.

On the side, I code prototypes to tell my own stories.
en.stat.titles: games shipped on console, PC, VR and mobile
en.shipped.title: Shipped titles
en.shipped.sub: Global Associate Producer at Bandai Namco Entertainment Europe, 2023 to 2025
en.shipped.ln3: The saga's big return. I followed production with Supermassive Games day to day, signed off deliverables milestone by milestone, and kept QA, analytics, localisation, marketing and communication in sync with development.
en.shipped.vr: The franchise steps into VR. I followed development so that scope, quality and the Little Nightmares identity held up next to the main game.
en.shipped.mob: The first game arrives on iOS and Android. I followed the port build after build up to launch, keeping the experience intact on mobile.
en.shipped.note: Developed with Supermassive Games and Iconik, ported with Playdigious and Engine Software, and tested with our playtest partners. A franchise that has passed 20 million copies sold across all games (Bandai Namco, June 2025).
en.craft.title: What I bring
en.craft.p.d: I hold schedules, see risks coming, make the call on scope and keep external studios moving. At Bandai Namco I rebuilt our entire project tracking on Jira, Confluence and SharePoint, and automated a report that used to cost a full day every week.
en.craft.d.d: I prototype fast and work on mechanics and on how the game feels, second by second. Accessibility is part of how I design, from the first prototype.
en.craft.t.d: I come from code. I read specs in detail, push back on estimates and speak the same language as engineers. I also automate business processes with Microsoft 365, Power Automate and SharePoint.
en.craft.e.d: At Ynov Campus I teach Producing, Game Design, Level Design and programming fundamentals, from first-year Bachelor to second-year Master. I also help studios organise their production and make their games more accessible.
en.career.title: Career
en.career.free.p1: When a production needs reinforcement, studios call me in. I take over coordination and reporting, set up their tracking tools (Jira, SharePoint, Teams) and structure the way the team works. On the design side I work on prototypes, mechanics and player experience, with accessibility as a common thread.
en.career.free.p2: I'm also Producer and Business Developer for the Hiqub collective. At Ynov Campus Lyon and Ynov Connect I teach Producing, Game Design, Level Design and programming fundamentals, from first-year Bachelor to second-year Master, and I consult.
en.career.bn.p1: Two years in the main team that drove the franchise's worldwide strategy. I ran three projects side by side, Little Nightmares III, Little Nightmares VR: Altered Echoes and the mobile port of the original, alongside Supermassive Games, Iconik and Playdigious, plus porting work with Engine Software.
en.career.bn.p2: My job was to keep everything on course. Milestones, deliveries, QA, analytics, localisation, marketing and communication had to move together, with clear reporting to stakeholders and IP holders. I rebuilt our tracking on Jira, Confluence and SharePoint, cut a full day of manual reporting every week through automation, and kept the scope consistent across the main game, VR and mobile.
en.career.nm.p: Six game projects, around forty people, one schedule to hold. I coached their project leads, and two years later some of them became my first clients.
en.career.ix.p: I automated business processes for our clients with Microsoft 365, Power Automate, SharePoint and Teams, then trained their teams until they could run it on their own.
en.career.boa.p: Interfaces and internal tools for the company's software, plus R&D on its processes. My first real steps as a developer.
en.edu.title: Education
en.proj.title: Own projects
en.proj.sub: My own games, from personal projects to game jams and school.
en.proj.najiki.d: A horror game I designed and produced. I took it to pitch competitions, and on Maghla's show it won funding support. The project is currently on hold.
en.proj.myhome.d: An escape game in Unreal Engine, made in my third year of Bachelor. I designed the puzzles and built the gameplay in Blueprints.
en.proj.market.d: A local party game for 1 to 4 players. The supermarket closes in two minutes and you have to grab everything before the others do. I was the technical game designer.
en.proj.mochi.d: A management game. A spaceship on its last legs, a crew of Mochis to direct, and food, water and oxygen to keep under control until arrival.
en.proj.ghost.d: A short roguelike made as a school project.
en.hk.title: The world of Hikali
en.hk.sub: Games and Japan don't stop at work. As Hikali, I share both in videos and live streams.
en.hk.lead: On my YouTube channel I am Hika I show Japan from the inside and the places every player dreams of visiting. I write, film and edit everything myself, and I stream on Twitch.
en.hk.soon: In the works, a series of interviews with game developers in Japan, starting with independent studios.
en.jp.title: Working in Japan
en.jp.big: For two years I was the bridge between a publisher and studios across Europe. Now I want to do that job in Tokyo, with Japanese teams.
en.jp.p: I live in Tokyo and I can start right away. I understand the vast majority of spoken Japanese and I'm at ease in everyday conversation. Reading and writing are catching up, with classes.
en.contact.title: Let's talk.
en.cp.title: Contact
en.cp.intro: A role to fill, a freelance mission, a YouTube collab with I am Hika or just a question? Write to me. I answer fast, in English, French or Japanese.

en.cp.ok: Thank you, your message has been sent. I'll reply soon.
en.cp.err: The message couldn't be sent. You can write to me directly at sabri.mohamadi@outlook.fr.
en.cp.activate: The form is being activated. In the meantime, please write to me directly at sabri.mohamadi@outlook.fr.
en.a11y.p1: At Bandai Namco Europe I was on the accessibility task force that worked on the publisher's accessibility strategy. I studied what the industry does best, from The Last of Us Part II to Tekken 8, mapped the options players need, and wrote the team's must-have accessibility document.
en.a11y.p2: On Little Nightmares I turned an accessibility audit into a prioritised backlog that the team shipped. Today I bring the same approach to the studios I advise and to my students.

fr.meta.title: Sabri Mohamadi | Producer & Game Designer
fr.hero.lead:
Deux ans dans la team principale de Little Nightmares chez Bandai Namco Entertainment Europe, en tant que Global Associate Producer. Trois jeux sortis, sur console, PC, VR et mobile.

Aujourd'hui, je suis Producer et Game Designer en freelance. J'enseigne le Producing, le Game Design, le Level Design et les bases de la programmation, du Bachelor 1 au Master 2.

À côté, je code mes propres prototypes pour raconter mes histoires.

fr.a11y.p1: Chez Bandai Namco Europe, j'ai fait partie de la task force accessibilité qui a travaillé sur la stratégie de l'éditeur. J'ai étudié ce que l'industrie fait de mieux, de The Last of Us Part II à Tekken 8, recensé les options dont les joueurs ont besoin et rédigé le document des must-have accessibilité de l'équipe.
fr.a11y.p2: Sur Little Nightmares, j'ai transformé un audit d'accessibilité en backlog priorisé, livré par l'équipe. Aujourd'hui, j'apporte la même démarche aux studios que j'accompagne et à mes étudiants.
